evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 112: sī mandātum neglēctūrus es (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to not heed, not trouble one’s self about … opp. to cūrāre”. Of a person, to slight him. The participle has a long ē by Lachmann’s law, as lēctus from legō.

terms.gloss: pass over, leave out, let go by
terms.comment: To let a thing go by unattended: a duty, a chance, a point in an argument (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: pretend not to notice, hide one’s awareness
terms.comment: Classically to disguise or hide, to make as if a thing were not so (Lewis & Short); so to ignore a remark on purpose. The sense “leave unnoticed” is late (Vegetius, Ammianus).

phrases.latin: subitō latrōnēs ex īnsidiīs advolant … dīripiunt nummōs, neglegunt vīle hordeum
phrases.english: suddenly robbers rush out of hiding … they seize the money and ignore the cheap barley

phrases.latin: propter suam impotentiam sē semper crēdunt negligī
phrases.english: because they are weak, they always think they are being ignored
